messages:
maria: Quick thread to finalize launch guardrails for Reserved Pools before I update the roadmap doc. Focus areas: burst model (time vs tokens), pro-rated billing for partial windows, emergency throttle behavior, and clear canary metrics.

kenji: Good list. My bias: token-bandwidth windows are easier for customers to reason about (seconds of burst -> tokens). But we can expose both semantics.

elaine: Sales asks: customers want predictable "burst headroom" numbers and simple pricing math. If we do pro-rata for partial windows we need an example in the pricing sheet.

maria: Proposed GA defaults: contiguous windows of 5 minutes (user-visible), token-based accounting, no carryover, pro-rata billing for partial windows only when customer upgrades mid-window.

tom_ops: Ops constraints: need an emergency-global-throttle that can be toggled cluster-wide to cap token ingress to X rps during incidents. Also require an audit log for manual overrides.

kenji: Implementation note: token-based ledger will track tokens_consumed per-tenant per-window and a rolling weighted-leaky-bucket fairness allocator will allocate leftover capacity every 30s. That grants proportional fairness across SLA tiers.

sarah: Runtime caveat: prewarm credits reduce initial KV-cache penalty. For GA default set prewarm_budget=1s per model instance; customers can buy extra credits.

maria: Acceptance criteria for GA canary:
- p95 generation latency delta < 7% vs baseline on reserved-pool traffic
- eviction_rate < 0.2% sustained
- billing snapshot export available to finance within 24h
- UI surfaces active window, remaining tokens, and last-eviction reason within 5s

product_lead: Canary plan: roll to 3% traffic, hold 72h. Measure p95, eviction reasons, autoscale churn. If any top-10 tenant sees >8% p95 regression, pause rollout.

elaine: For pricing sheet example please include: customer A has 600s monthly burst at N tokens/sec => shows prorated charge when they upgrade mid-month.

kenji: Telemetry names proposal (OTLP): ri.dedicated.burst_tokens{tenant,pool}, ri.dedicated.window_active{pool}, ri.dedicated.eviction{tenant,pool,reason}. Keep label cardinality low.

ops-bot: /event-schema create: eviction_event_v1 -> tenant_id,pool_id,ts,reason,active_tokens:int,fallback_model,operator_override:bool :white_check_mark:

tom_ops: Alert rules suggestion: P1 if global emergency throttle engaged >1min; P1 if evictions_rate >0.5% for 15m; P2 if billing export fails >1h.

sarah: Autoscale trigger tweaks: prefer queue-based triggers but backstop with token-rate delta. Proposal: scale_up when queue_len > 300 for 90s OR token_rate_delta > 2.5x for 45s. Add 4-window confirmation to avoid oscillation.

maria: UX ask: devex, show recommended client retry: 429 -> exponential backoff starting at 200ms, jitter up to 500ms, max retry window 30s. Add snippet in support docs.

kenji: Quick config example for PRD:
```
reserved_pools:
  window_seconds: 300
  accounting: tokens
  prewarm_budget_s: 1
  emergency_throttle_rps: 10000
  fairness: weighted_leaky_bucket
```

maria: Open questions I need resolved today: 1) pro-rata billing rules for upgrades/downgrades? 2) exact emergency_throttle default? 3) whether to allow fragmented internal credit use (hidden ledger) for advanced customers?

product_lead: Decisions: 1) pro-rata for upgrades only (simple); downgrades apply next billing cycle. 2) emergency_throttle default=global_rps*0.5 (ops can override). 3) hide fragmented ledger for GA, expose via contract.

tom_ops: I'll add emergency toggle + audit log implementation to ops backlog and propose UI admin flow.

elaine: I'll draft the pricing example and a short blurb for sales that explains pro-rata and no-carryover GA rule.

maria: Thanks. I'll update roadmap PR with these defaults and the canary plan. If folks agree, I'll mark owners: telemetry=kenji, runtime=sarah, ops=tom_ops, sales=elaine, product=maria. Flag objections here by EOD. :thumbsup:
